claims.text: Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 can remain incompletely densified with substantial residual porosity.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has insufficient strength or structural integrity during prolonged liquid-plating service.
Adding approximately 1–3 at.% Si to ZrB2 precursor powder enables transient liquid-phase sintering at approximately 1900–2100 °C.
Si addition lowers the effective liquidus temperature of the ZrB2-containing system.
The Si dopant forms a transient Si-rich liquid, likely a borosilicate phase, during sintering.
The proposed Si-rich liquid wets ZrB2 particle boundaries.
The transient liquid promotes particle rearrangement and capillary-driven densification.
Transient liquid-phase sintering improves intergrain bonding and reduces residual pore formation.
Reduced residual porosity makes ZrB2 less susceptible to corrosion-induced holes and eventual failure during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 2000 °C will have lower porosity than conventionally prepared ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 2000 °C will have higher mechanical strength, fracture toughness, and hardness than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 2000 °C will have significantly better corrosion and degradation resistance in a liquid plating bath than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
A sintering temperature of approximately 1900 °C or higher is required to form and maintain the ZrB2 phase in the proposed process.
The Si concentration must remain low to avoid unwanted secondary phases that could impair intrinsic properties.
The intervention is applicable to ZrB2 ceramics intended for high-temperature, corrosive service environments.

contradictions.description: The predicted comparison is against conventional undoped ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C, but the experiment sinters the undoped control at approximately 2000 °C. It therefore does not directly test the stated performance comparison or the asserted conventional baseline.
